incident-bot: [ALERT] 2801234567 — model-family=cicero-15b | metric=5xx_token_rate↑ | 95p_latency=2.60s | auto-shed=triggered? link=https://dash.redwood.ai/alerts/2801234567

maya (oncall): I'm on it. Paging @sam @eli. Customers reporting truncated streaming and 503s on some routes. Will triage impact and propose mitigations.

sam (sre): grabbing traces now. early look: high decoder queue length on cg-rt-7 and cg-rt-9, sustained TPM spike from a handful of tenants (~3). also some KV cache evictions.

eli (runtime): runtime note: we have multiple long-context requests driving kvcache growth + GPU mem pressure on a subset of nodes. decoder workers are ~90% memory. streaming piece exacerbates backpressure.

maya (oncall): quick options: 1) temporary family-level quota carve (RPM/TPM) 2) route % of traffic to cicero-15b-quant (lower mem) 3) disable streaming for non-enterprise tiers 4) per-tenant soft caps for top callers 5) emergency GC/kvcache flush (risky). Thoughts?

sam (sre): I support rapid quota reduce first. low blast radius, reversible. I'll apply a conservative cut: RPM -> 40, TPM -> 400 for family cicero-15b. Doing adminctl and will comment below.

sam (sre): ```
# admin command (internal)
adminctl set-quota --model-family cicero-15b --rpm 40 --tpm 400 --reason "live mitigation 2801234567"
```

admin-bot: Command received: `adminctl set-quota --model-family cicero-15b --rpm 40 --tpm 400 --reason "live mitigation 2801234567"`. Applying...

admin-bot: Quota change success: cicero-15b {rpm: 40, tpm: 400} applied to pool=hosted-us-west at 2801234582. Change-id: qc-2801-9a2.

eli (runtime): starting traffic-shift policy "fallback-quant-20" to send 20% of requests to cicero-15b-quant. Will monitor memory pressure.

deploy-bot: Rollout started: fallback-quant-20 -> routing rule applied to host pools [cg-rt-7,cg-rt-9] at 2801234620.

maya (oncall): additionally disabling streaming for non-enterprise keys to drop overhead. Commanding feature-toggle change now.

sam (sre): applying per-tenant soft cap to heavy callers. Targeting tenant AcmeWidgets (id: ten-883) softcap=30rps to reduce burst.

sam (sre): ```
# per-tenant cap
adminctl set-tenant-cap --tenant-id ten-883 --rps 30 --tpm 900 --note "mitigation 2801234567"
```

admin-bot: Tenant cap applied: ten-883 rps=30 tpm=900. Incident link: INC-2801-3612.

support-bot: Created customer incident INC-2026-3612 for AcmeWidgets; channel created with CS. Contact assigned: toni.

toni (cs): On it — posting brief to Acme AEs and adding an update to status.redwood.ai. I'll mention degraded streaming and potential rate limits.

maya (oncall): initial metrics: errors (5xx-token) trending down since quota change. 95p latency reduced from 2.6s -> ~1.0s median over last 2m. still watching.

sam (sre): traces look better. node mem pressure reduced on cg-rt-7. quant fallback serving OK but quality drop noted in a few evals — acceptable for mitigation.

eli (runtime): note: if we keep traffic-shift >25% we see slight regressions in overall latency due to smaller model context; currently fine at 20%.

maya (oncall): next steps: keep quota carve in place for 30m, monitor error rate and customer impact. If stable, we can gradually relax to rpm=60/tpm=800. If regression, rollback to previous config and escalate.

maya (oncall): handing off to @jordan for overnight watch. Jordan — TL;DR: cicero-15b hit memory+kvcache pressure from long contexts; we applied family-level RPM/TPM cut (40/400), 20% fallback to quant variant, disabled streaming for non-enterprise, and applied per-tenant cap to top caller AcmeWidgets. Customer incident INC-2026-3612 opened.

jordan (oncall): got it, taking over. I'll monitor dashboards, keep the carve for now, and will escalate to SRE lead if errors rise >1.5x baseline. ping me for any urgent console changes.

maya (oncall): thanks team. Leaving channel open, will follow up with a short post-incident note tomorrow. :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: NOTE: mitigation actions logged under change-ids [qc-2801-9a2, tc-2801-4b7]. Thread remains open until next update.
